# مصطفى السيد: نتواصل مع وزارة الصحة لإقرار تطبيق علاج السرطان بالذهب على البشر

الأحد، 03 مارس 2019 01:58 م

Image: مصطفى السيد: نتواصل مع وزارة الصحة لإقرار تطبيق علاج السرطان بالذهب على البشر الدكتور مصطفى السيد

(أ ش أ)

أكد العالم المصرى الدكتور مصطفى السيد أنه يتم حاليا التواصل مع وزارة الصحة بصفة مستمرة لعرض نتائج تجارب استخدام جزيئات الذهب النانومترية فى علاج السرطان والرد على كافة استفساراتها، والتأكد من أن تلك الجزيئات لا تؤثر سلبيا على خلايا الجسم السليمة، لإقرار تلك الطريقة والبدء فى تطبيقها على البشر.

جاء ذلك خلال المحاضرة التى ألقاها الدكتور السيد، اليوم الأحد، فى الصالون العلمى لأكاديمية البحث العلمى والتكنولوجيا لعرض أحدث تطورات أبحاثه فى علاج السرطان بجزيئات الذهب النانومترية، وبدء إجراء تجارب سريرية لهذا النوع من العلاج، بحضور عدد كبير من طلاب الكليات العلمية والصيادلة ونخبة من أساتذة الجامعات والمراكز البحثية.

وعرض العالم المصرى فكرة علاج السرطان بجزيئات الذهب النانومترية القائمة على حقن قطع الذهب الصغيرة (نانو) داخل الجسم لتمتص الضوء تحت الأحمر وتسخن الخلية السرطانية للقضاء عليها، موضحا أن التجارب أثبتت أنه عقب تسخين قطع ذهب ورفع درجة الحرارة حول الخلية يتم انصهار أو "تسييح" الخلايا السرطانية والبروتينات حولها مما يمنع انتشارها فى باقى أجزاء الجسم، مؤكدا أن التجارب مستمرة لمعرفة طريقة تغير عمل الخلية السرطانية بعد اعتيادها على تلك الطريقة.

وأشار إلى أن أكاديمية البحث العلمى قامت بتوفير التمويل اللازم لاستكمال الأبحاث على عدد كبير من حيوانات التجارب (قطط وكلاب وأحصنة) بجامعة القاهرة، موضحا أنه كان من قبل يتم استئصال الورم فى الحيوانات ثم يعود للظهور مرة أخرى بعد عدة أشهر، لكن الذين تم علاجهم باستخدام نانو الذهب لم يعد إليهم الورم مرة أخرى، حيث ثبت أنه يمنع انتشار المرض فى أجزاء الجسم ولا يؤثر على الخلايا السليمة.

وقال الدكتور مصطفى السيد "إنه لا يوجد تأثير سلبى على الجسم من ذرات الذهب، ولكنها تترسب فى الكلى والكبد، ومن خلال التجارب تبين أنها لم تسبب أى تأثير سلبى على الحيوانات على مدار 5 سنوات، ومازالت التجارب مستمرة.. لافتا إلى أنه فى الولايات المتحدة الأمريكية تم تطبيق طريقة مشابهة لجزيئات الذهب النانومترية لعلاج السرطان على البشر".

ونوه إلى أن البحث العلمى سيقود قاطرة التنمية فى مصر خلال الفترة المقبلة ويدعم الاقتصاد الوطني، مشيرا إلى أن العقول المصرية أثبتت مهاراتها عبر التاريخ فى مختلف المجالات، فمازال لغز بناء الأهرامات يحير العالم حتى الآن.

ومن جانبه، أشار الدكتور محمود صقر رئيس الأكاديمية إلى أن الصالون العلمى للأكاديمية يأتى ضمن فعاليات شهر العلوم المصري، الذى انطلقت فعالياته أمس وتنظمه الأكاديمية للعام السادس على التوالي، موضحا أن الصالون سيستضيف شهريا أحد كبار العلماء المصريين والعرب لمناقشة قضية علمية ملحة، وذلك تحت رعاية الدكتور خالد عبد الغفار وزير التعليم العالى والبحث العلمي.

وعقب المحاضرة، كرم الدكتور محمود صقر العالم المصرى الدكتور مصطفى السيد ومنحه درع الأكاديمية تقديرا لجهوده فى مجال البحث العلمى ودعمه المستمر لفعاليات الأكاديمية.

El-Sisi declared that Egypt will “carry out any measure to protect” Saudi Arabia, in a speech on Saturday, but said that he “hopes” the parliament will give him authorisation to proceed.

On Sunday, Egypt said it would provide “all necessary and possible support to Saudi Arabia to defend its safety and stability”. The National Defence Council, chaired by President el-Sisi, said it “stands fully with” Saudi Arabia to defend its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites.

But what would Egyptian assistance look like? And what capacity does it have to “protect” Saudi Arabia in its war with the Houthis?

Here is what we know.

## What’s behind el-Sisi’s decision to offer help to Saudi Arabia?

Saudi Arabia has long been a strategic and economic partner of Egypt, and el-Sisi said in a statement last month that Saudi security is “integral” to Egypt’s security.

Political analyst and Gulf studies expert Thomas Bonnie James told Al Jazeera that the Houthi security threat to the kingdom is one of the “converging” pressures that have led to this decision. The other one, is economics.

“Houthi pressure on [Bab] al-Mandeb threatens the Suez Canal, which Egypt’s foreign minister says has lost about $11bn since the attacks began in 2023,” he said, referring to Houthi attacks on Israeli-linked ships passing through the narrow strait, carried out in solidarity with Gaza.

James suggested that the decision is also important to Cairo, because “millions of Egyptians live and work in Saudi Arabia, which is Egypt’s largest single source of remittances. An Egyptian resident was killed, and others were injured in the attacks on Riyadh’s airport.”

The EBRD has been investing in Egypt since 2012

In Egypt, we focus on modernising the financial sector, developing the agribusiness sector and municipal and infrastructure projects, and upgrading transport and telecommunications services.

### An Egyptian success story: how EBRD investment is helping to improve wastewater services for Fayoum's rural inhabitants by building new treatment facilities and increasing the capacity of existing wastewater plants.

## Focus areas

### Promoting a more inclusive economy

The Bank seeks to promote a more inclusive economy for Egyptian businesses, women and youth, working to increase access to finance, entrepreneurship and skills development, as well as to services and economic opportunities.

### Accelerating Egypt’s green economy transition

The EBRD aims to help increase renewable energy capacity and develop a more diversified energy mix, improving the quality, efficiency and environmental sustainability of infrastructure, and promoting energy and resource efficiency and climate resilience.

### Enhancing Egypt’s competitiveness

We work to support private-sector growth and strengthen governance through a more expansive, competitive and resilient private sector; a deeper and more diversified financial sector and a broader array of financial products; increased private-sector participation; better governance; and an improved business environment.

Egypt became an EBRD recipient country on 30 October 2015. The EBRD's latest country strategy for Egypt was adopted on 9 February 2022.

The Bank’s portfolio in Egypt reflects a dual focus on sustainability and inclusion, with more than half of its investment volume going to green financing in 2025 and close to a third targeting greater economic inclusion. Green and inclusive credit lines, as well as risk-sharing facilities, play a central role, advancing decarbonisation and the competitiveness of firms through on lending to small and medium-sized enterprises and women entrepreneurs for growth and green investments. Alongside this, efforts to diversify the financial sector continue, including support for trade and supply-chain finance to strengthen economic resilience.

W hen Israel’s leaders gathered in Jerusalem on September 26, 2023, to mark the 50th anniversary of the Yom Kippur War, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described the surprise assault by Syria and Egypt as a cautionary tale, one of missed intelligence warnings and self-delusion. “We do not underestimate any threat,” he said.

Egypt,^{[e]} officially the Arab Republic of Egypt, is a country spanning the northeast corner of Africa and southwest corner of Asia via the Sinai Peninsula. It is bordered by the Mediterranean Sea to the north, Palestine and Israel to the northeast, the Red Sea to the east, Sudan and the Sahara to the south, and Libya to the west. The Gulf of Aqaba in the northeast separates Egypt from Jordan and Saudi Arabia. 【turn917academia14】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 6 days ago; 
Title: Morphology-aware deep learning predicts colorectal cancer survival from whole-slide images
Authors: Hikmat Khan, Metin N. Gurcan, Anil Parwani, Wendy L. Frankel, Wei Chen, Muhammad Khalid Khan Niazi
Date: Tue Oct 13 02:22:42 2026

Background: Five-year survival prediction from hematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide images could support risk stratification, but the task is weakly supervised, and the tissue morphologies carrying prognostic information remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We conducted a retrospective secondary analysis using TCGA-COAD/READ (n=562) for morphology-specific analysis, Alliance/ CALGB 89803 (n=424) for model development, and SurGen (n=218) for external evaluation. We propose MorphContrast, a morphology-aware contrastive multiple-instance learning framework that uses tissue labels as structural supervision for five-year survival prediction. MorphContrast combines gated-attention pooling with three auxiliary objectives: patch-level morphology labels define within-patient contrasts, outcome concordance or discordance defines cross-patient contrasts within matched morphologies, and diversity regularization discourages representational collapse. Morphology-matched patches from patients with discordant outcomes serve as hard negatives, encouraging prognostic discrimination within comparable histologic contexts. Results: Morphology-specific models show weak but distributed prognostic discrimination: adipose tissue achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.622, stroma achieves 0.604, and both perform comparably to tumor epithelium (0.601-0.605). On Alliance/CALGB 89803, the single model achieves an AUC of 0.642, while the post hoc ensemble reaches a pooled out-of-fold AUC of 0.70 and a risk-group hazard ratio of 3.79 (95% confidence interval: 2.55-5.63). On the external SurGen colon cancer cohort (n=218), the single model and ensemble achieve AUCs of 0.669 and 0.678, respectively. Conclusions: These findings support tissue morphology as structural supervision for outcome-aware representation learning in colorectal cancer prognosis.

Title: HexaBee-4B: Six-Language Translation with Multilingual Answering and Bidirectional Supervision
Authors: Iman Barati, Mohammadmostafa Rostamkhani, Mohammad Badzohreh
Date: Mon Oct 12 08:15:08 2026

Multilingual translation requires a model to preserve meaning while producing text in a requested language. We present HexaBee-4B, a translator adapted from Gemma 3 4B IT through three stages: Wikipedia continued pretraining, joint multilingual answering and answer-text translation, and bidirectional translation specialization. The intermediate stage connects two tasks through shared multilingual answers: answering a question in the requested language and translating an answer into that language. It comprises 19.46 million answering records, including 5.76 million cross-language question-answer pairs, and 10.70 million answer-text translations. The final stage uses 658,274 forward and reverse synthetic translation examples. On 36,572 synthetic test examples spanning all 30 directions among Arabic, Chinese, English, Hebrew, Persian, and Spanish, HexaBee-4B achieves direction-macro chrF++ of 73.75, compared with 57.11 for Gemma 3 4B IT and 66.83 for Gemma 3 12B IT. BLEU, TER, COMET, and a matched model-judged subset support the same overall ranking. These results demonstrate improved translation across the six-language set, with chrF++ gains in every evaluated direction over both baselines.

Chemistry evaluation has moved past multiple-choice probes toward open-ended expert problems, yet the benchmarks that define the current frontier still score answer endpoints alone. Such scoring conflates memorized facts with stepwise derivation, treats visual and textual inputs as interchangeable, and confounds long-horizon planning with stepwise execution. These blind spots prevent any diagnosis of where the reasoning chain breaks in a model. We present ChemArgus, a competition-level chemistry benchmark drawn from chemistry competition material, textbooks, and research papers, whose scoring replaces the answer endpoint with three measurement properties.
